name: Dukhan Bank
founded: 2008 (incorporated as Barwa Bank on 28 Jan 2008; operations began 1 Feb 2009; merged with International Bank of Qatar effective 21 Apr 2019; renamed Dukhan Bank Oct 2020; converted to Q.P.S.C. and listed on QSE 21 Feb 2023)
ownership_summary: QSE-listed since 21 Feb 2023. At 30 Sep 2026 the General Retirement and Social Insurance Authority held 24.48%, the Military Pension Fund (Qatar) 11.67% and Qatar Holding (QIA) 6.77% (interim statements note 1). The Sep 2026 investor presentation shows founders 66.5% (including Government 43.0%) and other shareholders 33.5%.

government_link: Yes - state pension funds (GRSIA 24.48%, Military Pension Fund 11.67%) and Qatar Holding (6.77%) at 30 Sep 2026 (S3); the investor presentation gives Government ownership of 43.0% and Government and GRE deposits of QAR 37.8bn (Sep 2026) (S7).
group_structure: Dukhan Bank Q.P.S.C. is the listed parent. It has 100% subsidiaries: The First Investor P.Q.S.C. (TFI, Qatar, 1999; Shari'a-compliant investment banking and asset management), First Finance Company P.Q.S.C. (Islamic financing), First Leasing Company P.Q.S.C. (Islamic leasing) and BB Islamic Derivatives (Cayman Islands, derivatives on behalf of the bank). It also holds an associate investment (QAR 14.5m). The bank reports four segments: Wholesale Banking, Retail and Private Banking ('including certain asset management activities for private customers'), Treasury and Investments, and Group Subsidiaries. TFI is not profiled separately, so its details are recorded here with scope 'Subsidiary: The First Investor'.

subsidiaries.name: The First Investor P.Q.S.C. (TFI)
subsidiaries.activity: Shari'a-compliant investment banking (financial advisory, ECM/DCM, M&A) and asset management (GCC equities, sukuk, money market, real estate and private equity)

subsidiaries.name: BB Islamic Derivatives
subsidiaries.activity: Derivative transactions on behalf of the bank (Cayman Islands)

footprint: Qatar only. Head office in Lusail Marina plus 8 branches (interim statements note 1, 30 Sep 2026). The investor presentation lists 9 branches including head office, 68 ATMs and 6 digital e-channels (Sep 2026).
customer_segments: Retail (mass), Prestige Banking (affluent: QAR 500k balance), Prime Banking (premium tier: QAR 2.5m deposits, QAR 75k monthly salary or QAR 4m non-salary financing), Private Banking (HNW), wholesale (corporates, government and institutional), plus investment-banking and asset-management clients of TFI.
business_lines: Four segments: Wholesale Banking (corporate, government and institutional financing, deposits, trade, cash management); Retail and Private Banking (financing, deposits, wealth management and advisory, cards, Thara'a prize savings account); Treasury and Investments (ALM, sukuk trading and market making, custody for sukuk investors, FX and Islamic hedging, structured investments, debt capital markets); Group Subsidiaries (TFI asset management and investment banking, First Finance, First Leasing). In 9M 2026, Retail and Private Banking produced 42% of income from financing and investing activities (QAR 4,232m in total).

capabilities.wealth_summary: Dukhan Bank's wealth business is Private Banking & Wealth Management, run by GM Chaouki Daher, who ran the same business at International Bank of Qatar. It sits in the Retail and Private Banking segment, which the bank says includes 'certain asset management activities for private customers'. Tiers are Prestige (affluent, QAR 500k balance), Prime (QAR 2.5m deposits, QAR 75k monthly salary or QAR 4m financing; offers advisory and discretionary portfolio management and succession planning) and Private Banking. Private Banking offers discretionary portfolio management in Qatar and GCC equities and sukuk, mutual funds (Qatar, GCC, regional and global), capital-protected products and sukuk. The bank held QAR 1.09bn of discretionary portfolios off balance sheet at 30 Sep 2026. The 100% subsidiary The First Investor (TFI) adds asset management (GCC equities, a sukuk fund, money market, real estate and PE funds) and investment banking. In Nov 2025 Dukhan signed an MoU with Global Infrastructure Partners (part of BlackRock) to be the exclusive distributor of GIP's Shariah-compliant private-market products in Qatar's consumer banking market. In Q3 2026 it signed an MoU with Lesha Bank on investment solutions. Global Finance named it World's Best Islamic Private Bank for the third year running (2026). No brokerage or in-app investing was found: Dukhan Mobile only lets Private and Prestige clients track their investments.

segments.name: Prestige Banking
segments.eligibility: Deposit and maintain a balance of QAR 500,000 or more (spouses also eligible). Dedicated RM and a Prestige Centre in each branch.

segments.name: Prime Banking
segments.eligibility: Any one of: minimum balance QAR 2.5 million across deposits; monthly salary of QAR 75,000+; or non-salary financing of QAR 4 million+. Includes Visa Infinite, advisory and discretionary portfolio management, and wealth planning.

segments.name: Private Banking
segments.eligibility: Not published. Clients get a Private Banker, a customised investment plan and Visa Infinite.

private_banking.detail: Private Banking & Wealth Management, run by GM Chaouki Daher. Offers a dedicated Private Banker, customised investment plans by risk appetite, portfolio management, mutual funds, capital-protected products, sukuk, private-banker cards (Visa Infinite), treasury and FX, and online banking. Named World's Best Islamic Private Bank by Global Finance in 2024, 2025 and 2026.

asset_management.detail: The First Investor (TFI, 100% subsidiary) does asset management across GCC Shari'a-compliant public equities, a global sukuk fund and segregated sukuk mandates, money market products, and alternatives (real estate funds in Saudi Arabia, Europe and Canada, and private equity). TFI's website claims 'over US$ 1 billion in assets under management' (undated). The bank also runs Discretionary Portfolio Management: QAR 1,090,875k off balance sheet at 30 Sep 2026.

brokerage.detail: No equity brokerage arm or brokerage service was found on the website or in the group structure. Treasury offers sukuk trading, market making and custody for sukuk investors, and TFI offers execution-only sukuk services through international custodians.

digital_investing.detail: Dukhan Mobile offers accounts, transfers (including international via Western Union), time deposits, cards and financing. Private and Prestige clients can 'track investments' but cannot buy them in the app. Euromoney named it Qatar's Best Islamic Digital Bank in 2026.

advisory.detail: Private Bankers build customised investment plans. The Prime tier offers 'Advisory & Discretionary Portfolio Management', local and global investment products, and retirement and succession planning with investment specialists.

discretionary.detail: 'Portfolio Management Services - Qatar, GCC equity markets and Sukuk, managed by a team of local and regional equity specialists'. Off-balance-sheet Discretionary Portfolio Management was QAR 1,254,401k at 31 Dec 2025 and QAR 1,090,875k at 30 Sep 2026.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No model portfolios or robo-advice found on the private banking, Prime or app pages or in the investor presentation.

funds_platform.detail: Private Banking offers 'Mutual funds - Qatar, GCC, Regional and Global funds across different asset classes'. No platform provider is named. TFI runs its own sukuk and money market funds.

structured_products.detail: Capital-protected products linked to equities, commodities and other assets for Private Banking clients. Treasury also offers structured investments linked to FX and to regional and international equities, with varying capital protection.

private_markets.detail: Under a Nov 2025 MoU (not yet a confirmed live product), Dukhan is to be the exclusive distributor of Global Infrastructure Partners' Shariah-compliant private-market products in Qatar's consumer banking market, for HNW and corporate investors, with joint product development planned. TFI runs real estate funds and private equity.

islamic_wealth.detail: All products are Shari'a-compliant: sukuk (Qatar, GCC, international), Shari'a-compliant GCC equity portfolios, funds, capital-protected products and Islamic hedging.

partners.partner: Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP), part of BlackRock
partners.what: MoU making Dukhan the exclusive distributor of GIP Shariah-compliant private-market products in Qatar's consumer banking market, plus joint product innovation and investor training
MoU to explore working together on investment solutions, signed in Q3 2026 (reported in the 9M 2026 release of 7 Oct 2026)
Strategic partnership to develop Open Banking use cases. Dibsy is in QCB's Express Regulatory Sandbox for Open Banking.

initiatives.what: 9M 2026 results: reported an MoU with Lesha Bank on investment solutions, joined the AFAQ GCC payments system, added Apple Pay and Samsung Wallet to Himyan, and won Euromoney Islamic Finance Awards 2026 as Qatar's Best Islamic Bank and Best Islamic Digital Bank.
Named World's Best Islamic Private Bank by Global Finance for the third year running. Chaouki Daher was the spokesperson.
Open-banking partnership with Dibsy announced at Web Summit Qatar 2026.
Exclusive MoU with Global Infrastructure Partners (BlackRock) to distribute Shariah-compliant private-market products to HNW and corporate clients in Qatar.
Prime Banking premium segment introduced (launch date not published). It offers advisory and discretionary portfolio management and wealth planning.

opportunities: Dukhan has an award-winning private bank (Global Finance World's Best Islamic Private Bank 2024-2026), but Dukhan Mobile only offers investment tracking, with no in-app buying of funds, sukuk or equities (S14, S15).
It is actively adding third-party investment shelf through partnerships: the GIP/BlackRock private-markets distribution MoU (Nov 2025) and the Lesha Bank investment-solutions MoU (Q3 2026) (S16, S6).
Discretionary portfolios are small and shrinking: QAR 1.25bn at end-2025 to QAR 1.09bn at 30 Sep 2026. Discretionary management is limited to Qatar and GCC equities and sukuk (S3, S9).
The new Prime tier (QAR 2.5m) promises advisory, discretionary management and wealth planning across 'local and global investment products' (S11).
barriers: Fully Islamic: all products need Shari'a board approval (S5 note 1).
Has an in-house asset manager (TFI) and treasury structuring capability, which may compete with external model portfolios and structured products (S19, S13).
The CEO has been acting since Jan 2023, and no head of digital or technology is named (S1, S18).
Relatively small client base (150k+ customers) and only 9 branches (S7).
incumbent_vendors: Global Infrastructure Partners (BlackRock) - private-markets products under MoU (S16)
Western Union - international transfers in Dukhan Mobile (S14)

discrepancies.detail: The FY2025 release headline gives a 'record annual profit of QAR 1.41 billion' (S8). The audited statements show net profit attributable to equity holders of QAR 1,258,068k after QAR 154,337k income tax; QAR 1,412,405k is profit before tax (S5). The presentation shows 'net profit before Pillar 2 tax' 1,411 and 'net profit' 1,258 (S7).
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded the audited figure after tax (QAR 1,258,068k). The QAR 1.41bn is a pre-Pillar-2-tax figure.

discrepancies.detail: The statements say 'head office ... and its 8 branches'. The presentation says 'Branches (incl. HO) 9'.
discrepancies.resolution: Consistent: 8 branches plus head office. Recorded 9 with that definition.

discrepancies.detail: Chaouki Daher is 'GM - Head of Private Banking & Wealth Management' on the website (S1) and 'General Manager, Head of Private Banking' in the presentation (S7). Abdulaziz Al-Neama is spelled 'Al-Naema' in S7. Ahmed Al-Emadi's bio calls him 'General Manager of Corporate Banking Services' while his heading reads 'GM-Head of Wholesale Banking'. The Governance Report 2025 uses 'GM – Head of Private Banking & Wealth Management' for Daher, 'Abdulaziz Al Neama' and 'Ahmad Abdulaziz Al Emadi' (S25).

The Governance Reports 2024 and 2025 list Faisal Kriez as Chief Technology Officer in the executive management (as of 31 Dec 2024 and 31 Dec 2025), but the website Management Team page (checked 12 Oct 2026) does not show him or any technology/digital executive.
discrepancies.resolution: Added with role_status 'Verified current' on the strength of the 2026-published Governance Report 2025; the website omission is noted. Confirm at the next check.

discrepancies.detail: Website bio: 'Master in Business Management and a Bachelor's Degree from Qatar University' (S1). Governance Reports 2024 and 2025: 'Bachelor's degree in Information Science and Media from Qatar University' with no master's degree mentioned (S26 p.23, S25 p.25).
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded the Governance Report wording (tier 1) and noted the website's additional master's degree.

discrepancies.detail: Website bio: 'Best Private Banker of the Year 2016' at The Banker Middle East Industry Awards (S1). Governance Report 2025: 'Best Private Banker of the Year' in 2016 and 2023 'in the Middle East and South Africa by MEED magazine' (S25 p.17).
discrepancies.resolution: Awards not recorded in the profile; noted here only.

discrepancies.field: Ahmed Hashem's last post before Acting CEO
discrepancies.detail: Jan 2023 announcement: 'Assistant General Manager of Wholesale Banking and Deputy CEO, the latest of which was' (S24). Website and Governance Reports mention only Assistant General Manager, Wholesale Banking / Corporate Banking Services (S1, S25, S26).

open_items: TFI leadership, current AUM and fund list were not found: the TFI website is stale (latest news 2016) and its 'over US$ 1 billion' AUM claim is undated.
Private Banking eligibility thresholds are not published. The Prime Banking launch date was not found.

Status of the GIP MoU (Nov 2025) and the Lesha Bank MoU (Q3 2026): no live product or distribution announcement found. The date and terms of the Lesha MoU were not published beyond the 9M 2026 release.

FY2025 annual report not located on the IR pages (checked 2026-10-12; the Annual Report 2024 is the latest PDF, S29). The Governance Report 2025 exists only as a Flipsnack flipbook; its text was taken from the flipbook page data (S25).
A PayLater MoU at Web Summit Qatar 2026 was seen in search snippets only and was not verified, so it is not recorded.

LinkedIn: official pages link only the bank's company page and the search tool declines name-based look-ups, so no personal profiles were verified (Hashem, Daher, Al-Neama, Jallad, Kriez: 'Not verified'; others 'Not checked').

Technology/digital head: Faisal Kriez is Chief Technology Officer (IT, PMO, digital transformation) per the Governance Reports 2024 and 2025 (S26, S25) but is absent from the website Management Team page (Oct 2026); confirm he remains in post. No separate head of digital banking or innovation is named anywhere.

Board term: the Governance Report 2025 states the current Board term runs 2023-2027 (nine non-independent members; next term 2028-2030 must have a majority of independent members) (S25 p.10). The Feb 2025 AGM agenda had no board election; the Chairman and Managing Director were elected/appointed by the Board (QSE notice 24 Feb 2025, S27).

The bank's 'Company Announcements' IR page renders no items without JavaScript; the 24 Feb 2025 QSE notice was read via The Group Securities' feed (S27). The bank's own press release on the chairman election was not found. A May 2023 item on the same feed (NEWS202305021549136157) reset the connection and was not read.
Khalid Al-Subeai (Advisor to the Chairman) appears on the website Board page but not in the Governance Report 2025; no biography or education published.

Shari'a Supervisory Board renewed for 2026-2028 at the 12 Apr 2026 AGM (Sheikh Dr. Walid Bin Hadi, Chairman; Sheikh Dr. Osama Qais Al-Dereai; Sheikh Dr. Esam Al-Enezy) (S28); members not profiled in this file.
